headline_marked: HC clears [[Sarowar Alamgir to take oath]] as Chattogram-2 MP
headline: HC clears Sarowar Alamgir to take oath as Chattogram-2 MP
summary: The High Court declared the Election Commission's decision to reject his nomination paper illegal, removing the obstacle to his swearing-in.
details: The High Court has cleared the way for BNP leader Sarowar Alamgir to take oath as a lawmaker from the Chattogram-2 (Fatikchhari) constituency.
The court declared the Election Commission’s decision to reject his nomination paper illegal, ruling in favor of the BNP leader.
The EC had previously rejected Sarowar's nomination on the grounds that he was a loan defaulter, a decision that was later challenged in court.
Following a writ petition filed by Sarowar, the High Court had issued a rule on January 27, asking the EC to explain the legality of its decision.
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court had previously suspended the publication of his election result until the High Court rule was disposed of.
The final judgment was delivered by a bench of Justice Fahmida Quader and Justice Md Ashif Hasan after hearing arguments from both sides.
caption:
A legal battle over a nomination paper ends in victory for BNP leader Sarowar Alamgir.

The High Court has cleared the way for BNP leader Sarowar Alamgir to take oath as a lawmaker from the Chattogram-2 (Fatikchhari) constituency.

The court declared the Election Commission’s decision to reject his nomination paper illegal, ruling in favor of the BNP leader.

The EC had previously rejected Sarowar's nomination on the grounds that he was a loan defaulter, a decision that was later challenged in court.

Following a writ petition filed by Sarowar, the High Court had issued a rule on January 27, asking the EC to explain the legality of its decision.

The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court had previously suspended the publication of his election result until the High Court rule was disposed of.

The final judgment was delivered by a bench of Justice Fahmida Quader and Justice Md Ashif Hasan after hearing arguments from both sides.

headline: 46,199 candidates: SC orders republication of results for primary teachers
summary: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has ordered the government to republish the results of 46,199 assistant teacher candidates based on merit, moving away from quota-based selection.
details: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh has ordered the republication of results for 46,199 candidates for the post of primary assistant teacher.
The court's ruling, delivered on Thursday, July 9, was led by the Chief Justice.
The results are to be republished republication based on merit rather than the quota system, which was previously used for these appointments.
According to senior lawyer Advocate Tajul Islam, the court issued the the directive to the government and relevant authorities following a writ petition regarding the quota system.
Previously, 84% of the primary school assistant teacher appointments and results were processed based on the quota system.
caption:
46,199 teacher candidates are getting a second chance. The Supreme Court has stepped in to ensure merit-based results.

The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh has ordered the republication of results for 46,199 candidates for the post of primary assistant teacher.

The court's ruling, delivered on Thursday, July 9, was led by the Chief Justice.

The results are to be republished republication based on merit rather than the quota system, which was previously used for these appointments.

According to senior lawyer Advocate Tajul Islam, the court issued the the directive to the government and relevant authorities following a writ petition regarding the quota system.

Previously, 84% of the primary school assistant teacher appointments and results were processed based on the quota system.
